items.caption:
Stripe CEO Patrick Collison says the number of new businesses starting on Stripe is up around 2x year over year.

He calls it the largest relative jump they have seen, and says it isn't just more lightweight projects: the median business is doing better than a year ago, and time to revenue for new Atlas companies is falling.

Is this really the best time ever to start a business?

Source: Y Combinator, Patrick Collison: Is AI Breaking the Lean Startup Playbook? Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=5d6y3poKwK4

items.caption:
Stripe CEO Patrick Collison says many of the most successful companies of the last 10 years are very anti-lean startup.

His point: 20 years ago, lean was almost the only option because of the capital available. With AI making it easier to spin up an organization, founders can now start far more aggressive and ambitious things up front.

Is lean startup advice outdated in the AI era?

items.caption:
Paul Graham says what actually motivates founders day to day is the fear of failure.

The dream of getting rich matters, but in the moment it's the fear of disaster or looking like a fool, like a server crashing. In his words, you just don't want your model train set to break.

Founders: is fear your fuel, or something you had to switch off?

Source: Y Combinator, Paul Graham On Startups, Ambition, and Great Founders. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=5bxp78i96S8

items.caption:
Paul Graham says that with startups, there's no easy major.

Early in YC's history, people started applying for the prestige, like getting into Harvard. But at Harvard you can slide through an easy major. A startup is like being forced to study theoretical physics: really rough unless you are very hard-working, clever and determined.

Would you start a company for the credential?

Source: Y Combinator, Paul Graham On Startups, Ambition, and Great Founders. Full video: youtube.com/watch?v=5bxp78i96S8
